seoTitle: Free MIME Type Lookup by File Extension
metaDescription: Find the MIME type for a file extension, or the extension for a MIME type, from a searchable list of web, image, audio, video and document formats. Free.
intro: Look up the MIME type for an extension like .webp, or work out the extension for a type like application/json. The list covers common web, image, audio, video, font and document formats.
why:
A wrong Content-Type is a classic cause of broken downloads and silent failures: fonts that do not load, scripts blocked by nosniff, a PDF that opens as text, a WebAssembly file that cannot be streamed. Remembering the exact type for every extension is unrealistic.

This lookup lists around a hundred extensions with the MIME type and a short description. Type an extension, part of a type or a word like "video" and the list narrows. Use it when setting up a web server, an upload validator or a storage bucket. It lists common types, so for anything exotic check the IANA registry.
howTo: Open the tool to see the whole list.
Type an extension such as .woff2, or part of a MIME type such as image/ or json.
Read the matching rows, which show extension, MIME type and description.
Copy the MIME type into your server configuration or upload rules.

faq.q: Is the correct JavaScript type text/javascript?
faq.a: Yes. The current standard type is text/javascript. The older application/javascript and application/x-javascript are obsolete aliases that you may still see, and servers should send text/javascript.

faq.q: Why do some extensions map to several types?
faq.a: Some formats have a registered type plus older aliases, and a few extensions are shared. For example .pem appears as a certificate type and as a generic PEM file. Choose the one your client expects.

faq.q: What should I send for an unknown file?
faq.a: Use application/octet-stream, which means arbitrary binary data. Browsers will usually offer to download it. Send a specific type whenever you know it, so the file opens properly.
